turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Come in, please. I will take the vitals, then the doctor will see you.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): File says thirty-four years. Correct?
[SEG0005] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I am his wife. Sorry, the auto got stuck at the signal, so we are late.
[SEG0006] person_1 (NURSE): That is fine. Arm out. Blood pressure is one twenty-eight over eighty-two.
[SEG0007] person_1 (NURSE): Pulse eighty-eight. Saturation ninety-eight percent.
[SEG0008] person_1 (NURSE): Temperature ninety-eight point six... no, hold still. It is a hundred and one point four.
[SEG0011] person_4 (DOCTOR): This itchy rash, since how many days?
[SEG0019] person_4 (DOCTOR): Swelling of the lips or the eyes?
[SEG0026] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): For the tooth. Ampicillin... actually no, amoxicillin. The dentist wrote amoxicillin.
[SEG0029] person_1 (NURSE): The slip says amoxicillin five hundred milligram, twice a day.
[SEG0030] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Our strip is two hundred and fifty milligram. He takes two hundred and fifty only, morning and night.
[SEG0031] person_4 (DOCTOR): Then the dose is not clear. I am not putting a number.
[SEG0033] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): From the medical shop. Betamethasone... no, the tube says mometasone. For the dry elbow.
[SEG0036] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sometime last week. Exact date I cannot say.
[SEG0039] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): At my sister's house, the day before the rash. He rarely takes prawns.
[SEG0040] person_4 (DOCTOR): Tablet, or cream, or prawns. Which one?
[SEG0044] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): In childhood, same type of rash. Penicillin injection, whole body became red and itchy. He was small only.
[SEG0045] person_4 (DOCTOR): Penicillin allergy, yes or no?
[SEG0047] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He does not remember, that is why. My mother-in-law told me. They avoided penicillin after that.
[SEG0048] person_4 (DOCTOR): I will keep your no, and her report. Both.
[SEG0051] person_4 (DOCTOR): Let me see. Red raised rash on both forearms and the abdomen. No blisters. Lips are not swollen.
[SEG0052] person_4 (DOCTOR): Chest is clear. Throat is mildly red, nothing else.
[SEG0053] person_4 (DOCTOR): Last night, did you feel hot? You said no fever.
[SEG0055] person_4 (DOCTOR): Loose motion, what about that?
[SEG0057] person_4 (DOCTOR): I cannot fix the cause today. This may be an allergic rash from the tablet or the prawns, or contact dermatitis from the cream. Either is possible.
[SEG0058] person_4 (DOCTOR): Stop the amoxicillin from today. Stop the mometasone also. No prawns till we know.
[SEG0059] person_4 (DOCTOR): I am starting cetirizine, ten milligram, by mouth, at night, for five days.
[SEG0060] person_4 (DOCTOR): If the rash is not better in one week, we can arrange a patch test. Not today.
[SEG0061] person_4 (DOCTOR): Come back after one week. If breathing gets tight, or the lips swell, go to emergency. Do not wait.
[SEG0063] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I will collect the tablet outside. Thank you, doctor.

spec.situation: Itchy rash after 'something I ate or the new cream or the antibiotic'; patient unsure which; a family member says the same happened with penicillin in childhood, patient denies. No firm diagnosis; patch test or antihistamine.
features: self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.
disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.

denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.

spoken_numbers: doses, vitals and durations are spoken as words or sloppy speech ('a hundred and two point five', 'one-forty over ninety', 'five-ish years', 'twenty milligram'); the label writes them normally (102.5, 140/90, 20 mg) and does not turn vague ones into exact ones.
